source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Indicate the date and time of inspection.
3. Record the name, I.D., and credentials of the inspector.
4. Document the location and name of the building.
5. Use standardized checklists.
6. Clearly note specific safety systems or components that did not meet safety standards.
7. Include information about the test conducted.
8. Add supporting details and any observed evidence.
9. Record any conversations with the property owner or building manager.
10. Photograph failed components or areas for visual documentation.
11. Note any immediate hazards and specify whether they were communicated to the building owner or relevant authorities.
12. Record follow-up actions required or advised.
13. Signature and stamp of the inspector.
14. Keep copies of inspection reports.
15. Maintain chain of custody for all records.
16. Archive all documentation according to local laws and regulations. 

By documenting failed inspections accurately and thoroughly, you provide both regulatory and legal protection, as well as ensure safety
